25.50000,42.70000.name: Domestic regulations that apply with respect to specific imports
25.50000,42.70000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
25.50000,42.70000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-84.35400,33.90360.name: Shady Grove Fertility-Atlanta
-84.35400,33.90360.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Desireé McCarthy-Keith, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-61.57631,16.23887.name: Inovie Biopôle Antilles
-61.57631,16.23887.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

12.16758,47.79907.name: Kathrinenhof Research Center (KRC)
12.16758,47.79907.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Boehringer Ingelheim Vetmedica GmbH. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-80.96392,46.46364.status: Preliminary Certificate of GAP Last visit: preliminary, July 2026
-80.96392,46.46364.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Preliminary Certificate of GAP Last visit: preliminary, July 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

126.63000,37.47000.name: Samsung Biologics
126.63000,37.47000.desc: One of the largest contract biologics manufacturers in the world, built by a Korean conglomerate in under two decades. Manufacturing capacity of this scale gives its owner a position in global medicine supply that no regulator granted and none oversees.

38.76000,9.03500.name: Ethiopian Biodiversity Institute
38.76000,9.03500.desc: Ethiopia’s national genebank, holding landraces of coffee, teff and other crops from a major centre of diversity. Material held here underpins breeding worldwide, and the terms on which it leaves are governed by treaties most people have never heard of.

-21.92000,64.13000.name: deCODE genetics (Amgen)
-21.92000,64.13000.desc: Holds genotype and health data covering a very large share of the Icelandic population, and has been owned by a US pharmaceutical company since 2012. A whole nation's genetics under one corporate owner is the arrangement every later biobank has had to define itself against.

-77.00530,38.89060.name: Monsanto Co. v. Geertson Seed Farms
-77.00530,38.89060.state: Washington DC — Supreme Court of the United States
-77.00530,38.89060.desc: The first engineered-crop case the US Supreme Court decided, in June 2010. Conventional alfalfa growers had shown that the Agriculture Department deregulated Roundup Ready alfalfa without the environmental impact statement the law required, and a district court enjoined all planting until one was done. The Supreme Court reversed the injunction 7–1 while leaving the underlying finding untouched: an agency breach of environmental law does not by itself entitle anyone to an injunction. The half worth keeping is the standing holding — the growers had it, because the district court found a reasonable probability that their crops would carry the engineered gene, and that risk injured them by itself. Justice Stevens, dissenting, set out the findings the majority did not dispute: the crop can reach other plants, it had done so even under controlled planting, and the agency had limited ability to monitor or enforce the limits it set.
